title: Reconstruction of human cognitive circuits after neurons have been lost

concept.text: This innovation would restore cognitive function by replacing neurons lost from an adult human brain and integrating the replacements into functioning circuits. The goal is to recover a computation impaired by neuronal death—for example, the ability to learn new information—and the everyday abilities that depend on it. Producing neurons or keeping a graft alive would be intermediate achievements; success would require the replacement cells to contribute to the recovered cognitive capacity. This is the target defined by the supplied materials, not a capability they demonstrate.

Conceptual synthesis: replacement must supply appropriate neuronal classes and connect them to an already organized brain. Depending on the damage, this could require rebuilding local cortical or hippocampal circuitry and reconnecting it with surviving networks. Amyloid clearance, dopamine replacement, axon repair and increased plasticity may support treatment or repair, but none alone establishes that replacement neurons have reconstructed a lost cognitive circuit.

significance.text: Conditional significance: if replacement neurons restored cognitive computations lost through neuronal death, the direct consequence would be recovery of the capacities those computations support. Sustained gains in new learning and independent daily function would represent a different therapeutic outcome from merely slowing further deterioration. Successful reconstruction could therefore change the prospects of people whose disability reflects neuronal loss, although its applicability would depend on the location and extent of damage and the condition of surviving circuitry.

Restoring the machinery of memory does not automatically restore the information once stored in it. Specific autobiographical memories could return only if enough relevant information survived elsewhere or could be independently reconstructed. Replacement neurons might enable new learning without recovering a person's lost life events. This distinction limits claims that circuit reconstruction would reverse every consequence of neurodegeneration or restore a prior mental state in full.

Conditional downstream possibilities include rehabilitation that uses restored learning capacity and repeated repair during a chronic disease. These possibilities would additionally require control of continuing pathology, durable integration and an acceptable treatment burden. The salamander-like regeneration analogy in the research notes can illustrate the ambition of replacing damaged tissue, but it does not establish that human cognitive circuitry or lost memory content can regenerate in the same way. The supplied evidence does not support a historical attribution for that analogy, and feasibility and timing remain highly uncertain.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central research challenge is to make appropriate replacement neurons restore a cognitive computation within an adult human brain after neuronal loss. The supplied animal report provides relevant evidence of tissue growth and nervous-system integration, but it does not establish this human outcome. Conversely, the limited evidence collection cannot establish that the target is absent from every part of the field as of 1 November 2026.

Engineering synthesis: concrete barriers include generating the required neuronal identities, delivering them to the appropriate sites, supporting survival and maturation, and establishing suitable incoming and outgoing connections. A replacement cell must participate in the relevant pattern of activity, rather than simply show neuronal markers or form some synapses. Repair may require coordinated reconstruction across several cell classes and regions; a surviving graft in one location would not by itself establish that this coordination has been achieved.

Scientific synthesis: an adult brain presents a different integration problem from tissue growing into an available space in an animal model. Researchers would need to determine how replacement cells acquire useful connections within surviving networks and how those networks learn to use them. In progressive neurodegeneration, repair must also remain effective despite the disease environment. Practical barriers include controlling excessive or inappropriate growth, maladaptive activity, immune responses and damage from delivery. These are proposed engineering concerns, not findings established by the retained source excerpt.

A further unresolved capability is convincing measurement of functional reconstruction. Structural evidence can identify cells and connections, but cognitive improvement could arise from effects on surviving neurons or other treatment mechanisms. Establishing the breakthrough therefore requires converging evidence that replacement neurons are functionally integrated and contribute to the recovered capacity, with causal tests where feasible and appropriate.

current_state.text: The reviewed portion of Max Kozlov's Nature news article, dated 16 September 2026, reports that transplanted human brain tissue can grow into much of the vacant space in mice lacking a key brain region and wire into their nervous systems. The caption identifies the absent region as cerebral cortex. This supports animal tissue-occupancy and integration groundwork. It does not establish restoration of cognition after adult human neuronal loss.

Access to that Nature article was partial: access options replaced most of the article in the retained copy, even though the extraction was not marked as truncated. The available material does not establish host age, how the cortex became absent, detailed experimental methods or cognitive restoration outcomes. The earlier description of neonatal mice filling a cortex that never developed therefore exceeds what the reviewed material supports. The news article lists a September 2026 Kaganovsky and colleagues paper with DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-11032-2, but its full text was not supplied for review.

The research notes also describe a 2022 study by Revah, Gore, Kelley and colleagues in Nature 610, 319–326, DOI 10.1038/s41586-022-05277-w. They report that human cortical organoid grafts integrated in developing rodent hosts and could influence reward-seeking behavior. No retained source artifact or source URL for that study was supplied for this review, so these details remain an attributed research-note summary. If confirmed, such behavioral participation would be relevant groundwork, while still leaving adult human cognitive reconstruction unestablished.

For lecanemab, the research notes identify van Dyck, Swanson, Aisen and colleagues, New England Journal of Medicine 388, 9–21 (2023), and report mean worsening on the Clinical Dementia Rating–Sum of Boxes at 18 months of 1.21 points with lecanemab and 1.66 with placebo. They also report amyloid-related imaging abnormalities with edema in 12.6%. Taken as reported, those results describe less decline while both groups worsened, rather than reversal of impairment. However, the source index contains no retained NEJM text, so the review could not independently verify the numbers, endpoint interpretation or adverse-event context. The missing artifact is an evidence limitation, not evidence that these reported results are false. Amyloid-treatment outcomes alone would not demonstrate reconstruction by replacement neurons.

The research notes describe a Brain review dated 3 September 2025 as covering a 12-person, uncontrolled phase 1 bemdaneprocel dopamine-cell trial. They attribute a modest response in the high-dose group and no significant accompanying change on 18F-DOPA PET imaging to that review. No retained Brain artifact was supplied, and the notes record difficulty reloading the page for full author confirmation. The trial design, clinical finding and PET statement therefore remain unverified here. As described, this is early, motor-focused dopamine-replacement work; even a confirmed motor benefit would not establish reconstruction of cortical or hippocampal cognitive circuits.

The supplied bounded-search record is empty, so the collection cannot support a comprehensive statement about the field as of 1 November 2026. Its dated reports remain relevant within their respective evidence limits. The reviewed material demonstrates neither achievement of the full human target nor its definitive absence across all current research.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: in people with documented neuronal loss from a neurodegenerative condition, an intervention produces sustained improvement in a prespecified cognitive capacity, such as new learning, together with improved independent daily function. The result should exceed merely slowing decline. A preregistered controlled design should address practice effects, changes in supportive care, symptomatic stimulation and other plausible explanations. These are proposed criteria for a convincing demonstration, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained cognitive recovery and improved independent function exceed slowing decline

completion_criteria.text: Proposed mechanistic evidence: validated imaging, tissue evidence where available, or other appropriate measurements identify replacement neurons of the relevant lost classes. Functional measurements should show useful synaptic integration, and converging evidence should link the replacement cells to the recovered capacity. Cell survival, anatomical connections or cognitive improvement alone would each leave important alternative explanations unresolved. Causal perturbation could strengthen the inference where ethically and technically feasible.
completion_criteria.label: Replacement neurons integrate synaptically and contribute to recovered cognition

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: demonstrate the effect across independent cohorts and, where feasible, independent centers; define the disease, severity, anatomical damage and patient characteristics for which it works; and follow durability, continuing neuronal loss, adverse growth, maladaptive activity and treatment burden. Follow-up duration and clinically meaningful improvement thresholds should be specified and justified for the application. Finite studies would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not universal repair of every cognitive circuit or neurodegenerative disease.
completion_criteria.label: Replicate effects across independent cohorts and report practical boundaries

completion_criteria.text: Recovery of particular autobiographical memories should be an additional outcome only where their information remains available or can be independently reconstructed. It should not be mandatory for demonstrating restored new-learning capacity. A Parkinson's motor-score improvement alone would not meet this cognitive-circuit criterion, and animal graft integration would remain an intermediate demonstration requiring further translation.
completion_criteria.label: Stronger: Recover autobiographical memories using available or reconstructable information

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: NEU-04, Content-faithful reading and writing of specific episodic memories, concerns the information carried by memories. NEU-06 concerns rebuilding the neuronal machinery that supports cognition. The two could overlap if reconstructing a circuit also required restoring specific memory content, but successful neuronal replacement need not recover lost autobiography, and writing a memory need not replace dead neurons.

Roster-based comparison: NEU-05, Target-specific regrowth of long axons in the adult mammalian central nervous system, could help replacement neurons reach the correct distant targets. Its central challenge can also arise in surviving neurons with damaged axons, without neuronal replacement. NEU-11, Reversible, circuit-specific reopening of critical-period plasticity in the adult brain, could help surviving and replacement cells reorganize their connections; increasing plasticity alone does not supply missing neurons. These entries retain distinct objectives despite their potential contribution to NEU-06.

Roster-based comparison: NEU-08, A generative developmental code that builds a specified functional neural circuit, overlaps the challenge of producing an organized replacement circuit. Its title does not require repair inside a damaged adult human brain. NEU-09, Cell-type-specific molecular access throughout the intact adult human brain, could support targeting, monitoring or control of relevant cells, but access alone would not reconstruct a lost computation.

Roster-based comparison: NEU-01's simultaneous spike-resolved recording, NEU-02's whole-brain synaptic connectomics and NEU-03's predictive theory of circuit computation could help measure, design or explain reconstruction. NEU-07's noninvasive cellular-resolution reading and writing could support assessment or control. These are potentially enabling capabilities with distinct endpoints; NEU-06 does not require that each be fully achieved before a bounded repair demonstration could succeed.

Roster-based comparison: NEU-10, A causal, measurement-grade account of conscious content, and NEU-12, An account of sleep sufficient to complete its necessary functions without a normal sleep period, address different explanatory and functional targets. Cognitive-circuit reconstruction could interact with conscious experience or sleep-dependent function, but the supplied titles provide no basis for treating either as equivalent to neuronal replacement. These comparisons use the supplied roster titles; detailed specifications for the other entries were not supplied.

unresolved_issues: The lecanemab endpoint values, both-group worsening interpretation and 12.6% edema figure need verification against retained primary-source text and their clinical context.
The bemdaneprocel trial size, control design, clinical response and reported absence of significant 18F-DOPA PET change remain unverified in this evidence package.
The 2022 organoid study's host conditions, integration measurements and behavioral results require its underlying source for verification.
The full 2026 Kaganovsky paper is needed to establish host age, model construction, experimental scope and functional outcomes; the partial news excerpt cannot resolve these details.
No bounded freshness search establishes the full state of adult human cognitive-circuit reconstruction as of 1 November 2026.
Clinically meaningful cognitive and daily-function thresholds, follow-up duration and feasible causal measurements remain application-specific proposals.
Detailed boundaries with neighboring concepts remain provisional because only their roster titles were supplied.

The review's recommendation to omit unverified clinical details from the factual account was adapted by retaining them as clearly attributed reports, because the requested consolidation calls for preserving useful quantitative detail with explicit uncertainty.

brief.title: Restoring thinking abilities by replacing lost brain cells
possible: People who have lost the ability to learn because brain cells have died could regain it. Replacement neurons—the cells that carry brain signals—would join surviving networks and help them work again.
Recovered learning could help people regain independence and benefit from rehabilitation.
why: For people disabled by brain-cell loss, recovering an ability would change daily life beyond what slowing further decline can achieve. Rebuilding the networks behind learning could restore capacities that continuing care depends on.

sources.who: Van Dyck, Swanson, Aisen and colleagues
sources.showed: This is a clinical study of lecanemab, a treatment targeting amyloid protein buildup in the brain.
sources.cited_for: The study provides a comparison with treatment aimed at slowing cognitive decline.
sources.not_established: Slower decline does not establish that replacement neurons rebuilt a lost brain network.

sources.showed: This is a review covering an early, uncontrolled trial of bemdaneprocel, a cell treatment intended to replace neurons that produce the chemical messenger dopamine.
sources.cited_for: The review covers cell replacement aimed at movement problems.
sources.not_established: Improved movement would not establish reconstruction of networks responsible for learning or memory.

sources.showed: Human brain tissue transplanted into mice missing a brain region grew into much of the empty space and connected to their nervous systems.
sources.quote: Human brain tissue transplanted into mice that lack a key part of their brains can grow to occupy most of the vacant space and wire into the animals’ nervous systems.
sources.cited_for: The work demonstrates tissue growth and connections between a human graft and an animal nervous system.
sources.not_established: It does not demonstrate recovered cognition after brain-cell loss in an adult human.

shown: Kaganovsky and colleagues have shown that transplanted human brain tissue can grow and connect inside mice missing the cerebral cortex, a brain region. This establishes groundwork for integration. Restoring an adult human’s lost thinking abilities through replacement neurons remains a further step.
missing: Replacement neurons must restore a lost thinking ability within an adult human brain.
The right kinds of replacement cells must form useful connections with surviving networks.
Measurements must establish that replacement cells contribute to recovery, beyond effects on surviving cells.
Repair must endure continuing disease without harmful growth, disruptive activity or unacceptable treatment burdens.

milestones.label: Sustained recovery of thinking and daily independence
milestones.explanation: A controlled study would have to show lasting gains in a defined thinking ability and independent daily function after brain-cell loss from degenerative disease. This would establish recovery beyond slower decline.

milestones.label: Replacement neurons help produce the recovered ability
milestones.explanation: Measurements would have to identify the needed replacement neurons, show working connections and link their activity to recovered cognition. This would establish that the new cells help produce the recovery.

milestones.label: Independent groups repeat recovery and establish its limits
milestones.explanation: Independent patient groups would have to show repeatable benefits, with durability, harms and patient eligibility defined. This would establish where repair works and its practical limits.

milestones.label: A further result restores particular personal memories
milestones.explanation: Particular personal memories would have to return where their information survives or can be independently reconstructed. This would go beyond restored new learning, which does not require old memories to return.

uncertain: Replacing the machinery for learning may not recover personal memories whose information has been lost.
The size and duration of gains needed to count as meaningful recovery remain application-specific.
How replacement neurons acquire useful connections in an organized adult brain remains unresolved.

page.title: Neuronal replacement for cognitive recovery
page.definition: Replacement neurons restore a cognitive ability lost through neuronal death in an adult human brain. The new cells have the required identities and functional synapses—the connections through which neurons signal—and contribute causally to the recovered ability.

goal.need: Dementia impairs memory, thinking and daily activities. WHO’s population, expenditure and informal-care estimates quantify the burden motivating attempts to restore cognition. Neuronal replacement addresses abilities lost through neuronal death; these burden estimates do not establish eligibility for this intervention.

figures.caption: Global dementia burden reported by WHO.
rows: Share of cost attributable to informal care
figures.note: These estimates concern dementia overall, not the population eligible for neuronal replacement.

statements.body: California Institute for Regenerative Medicine; funded StemCells, Inc.–University of California, Irvine Disease Team
statements.quote: We propose to evaluate the use of human neural stem cells as a potential innovative therapy for AD.
statements.context: AD means Alzheimer disease. Grant DR2A-05416 pursued memory restoration, including possible growth-factor-mediated protection; it did not require neuronal replacement as the mechanism.

statements.quote: Preclinical studies are ongoing to investigate whether NRTX-1001 can repair neural activity in the temporal lobes, reduce neurodegeneration, and improve cognition.
statements.context: The Alzheimer disease programme uses stem-cell-derived inhibitory neurons.

completion.title: Replacement neurons causally restore lost cognition in adults with neuronal loss.
completion.criterion: In adults with acquired neuronal loss and a corresponding cognitive deficit, a controlled study demonstrates recovery of a prespecified impaired ability: improvement from pretreatment baseline and against concurrent controls, with benefit in related daily functioning. Converging evidence identifies replacement neurons, establishes their functional input and output connections, and attributes a causal contribution to them. Outcomes, clinically meaningful effect sizes and follow-up must be justified for the indication; no universal numerical cutoff is established.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; an explicit synthesis because no external completion criterion for this capability was located.
completion.basis: Searches of FDA Alzheimer guidance, ISSCR translation guidelines, CIRM programme milestones, neuronal-replacement reviews and the NRTX-1001 programme found no published completion test for human cognitive-circuit replacement. This test combines the cognitive goal, the field’s identity-and-connectivity requirement and its causal-perturbation convention; it adds no universal score or follow-up cutoff.

milestones.title: Replacement neurons acquire the required identity and functional host inputs and outputs.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate the required neuronal subtype and functional incoming and outgoing connections in a recipient brain. The field defines replacement by identity and connectivity, without a universal cell-count threshold. In adult mice after traumatic brain injury, Zhu and colleagues recorded mature interneuron properties and excitatory inputs in 10 grafted cells from 3 mice at 45–60 days after transplantation; host inhibitory currents were assessed in 13 cells from 3 grafted mice, versus 12 cells from 3 injured controls and 11 cells from 3 uninjured controls.
milestones.set_by: Neuronal-replacement field; biological criteria articulated by Götz and Bocchi in their 2021 review.
milestones.threshold_quote: Adequate identity and connectivity is a prerequisite to restore neuronal network function

milestones.title: A neural-cell intervention produces significant, consistent memory improvement in relevant animal models.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate significant, robust and consistent memory improvement in the disease-relevant animal studies specified by the programme. CIRM’s DR2A-05416 report describes 3 animal studies and says increased hippocampal connections did not consistently improve memory; the programme failed its scientific gate and the loan was terminated in 2014. Animal sample sizes and the numerical decision boundary are not disclosed. This was an Alzheimer disease neural-stem-cell programme, not proof that graft-derived neurons mediated recovery.
milestones.set_by: CIRM, grant DR2A-05416 scientific go/no-go milestones, described in its second-year report; this threshold was written for Alzheimer disease models.

milestones.title: Silencing replacement neurons reverses an animal’s recovered cognitive performance.
milestones.criterion: After cognitive improvement in an injured or diseased adult animal, selectively suppress graft-neuron activity and test whether recovered performance is lost, with controls for the perturbation. Zhu and colleagues demonstrated reversal of improved memory precision after traumatic brain injury in mice: 5 graft recipients, 7 injured controls and 8 uninjured controls. Upadhya and colleagues found that silencing human graft-derived interneurons impaired object-location memory in chronically epileptic rats; the graft group comprised 6 rats. These are task-specific causal demonstrations.
milestones.set_by: Neural-transplantation field’s graft-activity perturbation convention, reviewed by Gonzalez-Ramos and colleagues; their quoted example concerns motor recovery, with cognitive applications demonstrated by Zhu and Upadhya.
milestones.threshold_quote: motor deficits were rapidly and reversibly re-introduced in recovered mice when grafted neurons were silenced by light

milestones.title: A neuronal replacement product is authorised to enter a human clinical trial.
milestones.criterion: The investigational new drug application becomes effective: normally 30 days after FDA receipt unless a clinical hold is imposed, or earlier on FDA notification. ISSCR also requires rigorous preclinical safety and efficacy before early human studies. On 4 November 2021, Neurona reported FDA clearance of NRTX-1001 for a first-in-human phase 1/2 trial in drug-resistant mesial temporal lobe epilepsy. The clearance report is a company announcement, not peer-reviewed evidence of cognitive recovery.
milestones.set_by: FDA investigational-new-drug procedures; the rule applies to investigational biological products generally. ISSCR recommendation 3.3.1.2 supplies the preceding preclinical safety-and-efficacy bar.
milestones.threshold_quote: 30 days after FDA receives the application, unless FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigations described in the application are subject to a Clinical Hold

milestones.title: Replacement neurons are transplanted into adults in an authorised clinical trial.
milestones.criterion: Deliver the neuronal product to adults under the authorised protocol. NCT05135091 specifies stereotactic hippocampal injection of NRTX-1001 in drug-resistant unilateral mesial temporal lobe epilepsy. On 22 April 2026, Neurona reported 31 participants dosed across its unilateral and bilateral phase 1/2 studies, with no serious adverse events attributed to the cells or administration procedure. These company-reported results are not peer reviewed; seizure outcomes and absence of group cognitive decline do not establish cognitive restoration.
milestones.set_by: Neurona Therapeutics, NCT05135091 phase 1/2 protocol as described in its 2023 study poster; this human-delivery milestone was specified for temporal lobe epilepsy.
milestones.threshold_quote: Cells are transplanted via stereotactic injection along the long axis of the hippocampus with intra-operative MRI imaging.

milestones.title: A neuronal replacement therapy benefits cognition and daily function in a controlled human trial.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate favorable treatment effects on both cognition and daily functioning, using separate assessments or an integrated scale that meaningfully measures both; compare the cell intervention with an appropriate available treatment. FDA published this outcome criterion for Stage 3 Alzheimer disease, with qualifications for early Stage 3. The guidance supplies no universal point-change or follow-up threshold. A relative benefit can precede proof of recovery from baseline and of the graft neurons’ causal contribution.
milestones.set_by: FDA’s March 2024 draft guidance, Stage 3 Alzheimer disease outcome criterion; nonbinding and not a universal criterion for other indications. ISSCR recommendation 3.4.5.1 specifies comparison with available therapeutic approaches.
milestones.threshold_quote: favorably affects the observed impairments in both cognition and daily functioning.

not_found: No controlled human neuronal-replacement study was found that demonstrated cognitive recovery and established the replacement neurons’ causal contribution.
CIRM’s public DR2A-05416 report does not disclose animal sample sizes or its numerical memory-performance decision boundary.
The supplied Nature news article and the Kaganovsky paper could not be opened successfully.
The supplied NEJM full text could not be opened successfully.

results.finding: Human brain tissue in mice lacking a cerebral cortex wired into their nervous systems; sample size not reported.
results.detail: The text does not establish the required neuronal subtype or functional incoming and outgoing connections.
results.quote: Human brain tissue transplanted into mice that lack a key part of their brains can grow to occupy most of the vacant space and wire into the animals’ nervous systems.

results.finding: In adult mice with traumatic brain injury, all 10 recorded grafted interneurons received excitatory inputs.
results.detail: At 45–60 days after transplantation, grafted cells showed mature interneuron properties. Inhibition was restored in host granule cells sampled from grafted mice, although those recordings did not directly identify the grafted cells as the source of each inhibitory current.
results.quote:
In slices from MGE-grafted mice containing GFP+ cells, IPSC frequency and kinetics were restored to control levels (
n
= 13 cells from 3 TBI-MGE mice).

results.finding: Human MGE-type interneuron grafts in epileptic mouse hippocampus received excitatory inputs in 4 of 5 recorded cells and produced inhibitory responses in 2 of 4 host cells.
results.detail: The grafts expressed GABAergic MGE interneuron markers. Input and output recordings were made about 15–16 months after transplantation; the output recordings were from one mouse. The subtype fate of some grafted cells remained undetermined.
results.quote: (Z) Average eIPSC amplitudes recorded from mouse neurons following blue light stimulation in the WT CTX (n = 5 out of 23 recorded cells from 4 mice, ~17 MPT) and in the epileptic HC (n = 2 out of 4 recorded cells from 1 mouse, ~16 MPT).

results.finding: Human neural stem cells in Alzheimer’s mouse models: 3 animal studies; sample sizes not disclosed; memory did not improve consistently.
results.detail: The programme reported no significant change in memory performance and did not meet its scientific gate. The loan was terminated in December 2014. The numerical decision boundary was not disclosed.
results.quote: Despite seeing a very exciting increase in the number of connections between key hippocampal neurons within the brains of mice treated with human neural stem cells, this did not appear to robustly and consistently improve memory in the animals.

results.finding: In 5xFAD mice (6–10 per group), transplanted interneurons improved novel object recognition at 3 months (p=0.0017).
results.detail: This is a separate study, not the animal studies specified by the CIRM programme. The authors also report no significant improvement in novel object recognition at 2 months.
results.quote: Overall, these results indicate that the transplantation of MGE‐pINs can improve cognitive behavioral deficits in 5xFAD mice without affecting general motor abilities, indicating no excess inhibition.

results.finding: In 5 grafted mice with traumatic brain injury, silencing transplanted neurons reversed improved contextual memory precision (P = 0.009).
results.detail: The experiment included 7 injured and 8 uninjured controls. Compound 21 had no overt effect on animals without grafts.
results.quote: Grafted animals had improvements in memory precision that were reversed by chemogenetic silencing of the transplanted neurons and a long-lasting reduction in spontaneous seizures.

results.finding: In 6 grafted epileptic rats, silencing graft-derived neurons abolished object-location discrimination (p > 0.05).
results.detail: Before silencing, grafted rats preferred the object in the novel location (p < 0.01). Exploration time, distance traveled, and velocity were comparable before and during silencing. Pattern separation remained intact.
results.quote:
Object location memory
was impaired in CERs with no grafts and CERs with grafts when graft-derived interneurons were silenced.

results.finding: NRTX-1001 received FDA IND clearance for a phase 1/2 trial; the first stage planned to enroll up to 10 people.
results.detail: The company announcement reports clearance; it does not establish cognitive recovery. No patients had yet been recruited when the release was issued.

results.finding: Neurona reported 31 participants dosed with NRTX-1001 across two phase 1/2 trials.
results.detail: The total combines unilateral and bilateral epilepsy studies. This company-reported result does not establish cognitive restoration.
results.quote: A total of 31 participants have been dosed across both studies with either a low or a high dose of rezanecel.

results.finding: After neuronal transplantation for basal ganglia stroke, 4 of 7 transplant recipients showed marked improvement on a visuospatial and memory test.
results.detail: Nine subjects completed testing, including two controls. The reported improvement was in the four transplant recipients with nondominant-hemisphere strokes; the text does not report daily functioning or a comparative treatment effect.
results.quote: Four transplanted subjects who had strokes in the nondominant hemisphere showed marked improvement on the Rey Complex Figure, a test of visuospatial/constructional ability and nonverbal memory.

results.finding: In 54 randomized Huntington’s disease patients, fetal cell grafts showed no functional capacity benefit at 20 months (P = 0.771).
results.detail: The delayed-start controlled trial found no benefit on cognitive or daily-function secondary outcomes; Stroop word performance declined more in the treated group. It therefore did not demonstrate favorable effects on both cognition and daily function.
